chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id or others, from Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"The evidence (shahada/testimony) in marriage was established solely for the sake of inheritance."

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: Evidence or testimony (specifically the declaration of marriage)

ai.seo_question: Why is testimony required for marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the juridical necessity of public testimony (bayyina) in marriage is fundamentally rooted in securing lineage (nasab) for inheritance distribution. This hadith, recorded in al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the pragmatic dimension of Shia family law, where the visibility of the contract prevents disputes over heirship and ensures the clear transmission of wealth according to divine shares.
